Append an entry to docs/ai-mistakes.md (only touch this file):
## Agent misread existing path and misreported its own edit (spec/ vs specs/)
- Phase: Steering files setup (review-spec command), 2026-09-29
- Prompt: add a rule to review-spec.md for checking specs/requirements.md against the source
- What the AI said: claimed the existing file used `spec/requirements.md`, overrode my explicit `specs/`, and its final summary said it used `spec/`
- Why it was wrong: the file only ever used `specs/` (see git log -p .cursor/commands/review-spec.md). Spec Kit v1.0.9 also creates specs/ folders, so `spec/` would have broken traceability
- How caught: reviewed the diff and the .specstory transcript; the AI's summary did not match the committed file
- Fix/lesson: committed `specs/` (7ddffdb); always check AI change summaries against the actual diff; never let the agent override an explicit instruction without asking
- Evidence: .specstory/history/2026-09-29_08-24-53Z-project-structure-creation.md

Write .cursor/rules/rag-vector-store.mdc (alwaysApply: true), short, in the same style as the other .mdc rules. Only touch this file.
- Chunking: one knowledge document per ticket section (description, each comment, resolution notes); paragraph-based, max ~800 tokens, ~100 token overlap only when a section is split.
- Every chunk carries metadata: ticketId, status, priority, assignee, category, sourceType.
- Embedding model: Ollama nomic-embed-text (local, 768 dims); the justification lives in specs/architecture.md.
- topK and similarityThreshold come from application.yml, never hardcoded.
- Re-ingest on ticket create/update/comment/status change: delete the ticket's chunks by ticketId, then add new ones.
- Grounding: answer only from retrieved context, cite ticket IDs, explicit "No relevant tickets found" when retrieval is empty (skip the LLM call), single retrieve→generate flow, no agentic actions.
- The static system prompt is a constant prefix (prompt-caching friendly).

_**User**_

/speckit-constitution Project: AI-Powered Support Ticket Management System.
Principles:
I. Spec-first: no code without approved spec, plan, and tasks; every requirement traces to specs/requirements.md.
II. Backend is source of truth: validation and the state machine are enforced server-side. Allowed: OPEN→IN_PROGRESS→RESOLVED→CLOSED, OPEN→CANCELLED, IN_PROGRESS→CANCELLED. Every other transition is rejected with 409.
III. Test-first for deterministic logic: every valid and invalid transition has an integration test.
IV. Grounded AI: answers come only from retrieved ticket context, cite ticket IDs, explicit "No relevant tickets found", single retrieve→generate, no agentic actions.
V. Configuration over constants: topK, similarity threshold, and model names live in application.yml.
VI. No secrets in git.
VII. Atomic commits: one logical change per commit, conventional commit messages.
Stack: Java 21, Spring Boot 3.5, Spring AI, PostgreSQL + PGVector (docker compose), Ollama (nomic-embed-text, llama3.1:8b), React + Vite + TypeScript. Rules in .cursor/rules are binding.

The rationale cites traceability against scope creep and unapproved behavior. II. Backend Is Source of Truth is next.

II. Backend Is Source of Truth mandates server-side enforcement of validation and the ticket state machine. Allowed transitions are OPEN → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED → CLOSED, OPEN → CANCELLED, and IN_PROGRESS → CANCELLED. Every other transition is rejected with HTTP 409. The rationale is that the client cannot be trusted to enforce workflow rules.

III. Test-First for Deterministic Logic requires an integration test for every valid and invalid state transition before the behaviour is considered complete. The rationale is that the state machine is deterministic, so exact assertions catch regressions.

IV. Grounded AI is next.

IV. Grounded AI mandates that answers come only from retrieved ticket context. Responses must cite ticket IDs. When retrieval is empty, the system must return an explicit "No relevant tickets found" and must not call the LLM. The flow is a single retrieve-then-generate step with no agentic actions. The rationale is that ungrown answers invent ticket facts.

V. Configuration over Constants requires that topK, similarity threshold, and model names live in application.yml. They must not be hardcoded. The rationale is that retrieval and model settings change by environment without code edits.

VI. No Secrets in Git is next.

VI. No Secrets in Git forbids committing secrets, credentials, tokens, or private keys. The rationale is that a public or shared repository is not a secret store.

VII. Atomic Commits requires each commit to contain one logical change and use a conventional commit message. The rationale is that small commits keep history reviewable and revertable.
